name: Bimetric-Khronon Slip MOND (BKSMOND)
claimed_mechanism: This candidate introduces a second dynamical metric coupled via a Hassan-Rosen ghost-free potential, which exits the DC-013 slip-lock by providing an off-ray helicity-0 source for the lensing. The MOND dynamics are encoded in a local auxiliary field chi. A degenerate (stiff) vector A_mu provides the preferred frame, with its coupling strictly screened by e^-y.
predicted_weak_field: In the Newtonian regime, the theory recovers GR. In the MOND regime, the MOND force law is recovered from the chi field. The bimetric sector provides the necessary lensing slip (Phi != Psi) that evades the DC-013 no-go. The screened vector coupling ensures that preferred-frame violations are exponentially suppressed in the Solar System.
inequivalence_argument: This candidate is inequivalent to DC-001 because it contains a preferred-frame coupling (via A_mu) and a second metric sector (exiting the single-metric constraint). It is inequivalent to DC-010 because the kinetic normalization of the vector A_mu is independent (degenerate/stiff) and not controlled by the screened coupling, avoiding the P7 strong coupling. It is inequivalent to DC-014 because the bimetric sector provides the lensing slip, not the stiff vector alone, and the vector is strictly screened.
